title: Feyenoord in the Champions League: Draw Sets Opponents and Challenges
subtitle: The Dutch club returns to Europe’s top competition with a new coach and a lineup of matches that promises intense drama.
excerpt: The UEFA Champions League 2026/27 draw spotlighted Feyenoord Rotterdam. With a challenging match schedule, the Dutch side is gearing up to face some of Europe’s.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The UEFA Champions League 2026/27 group stage draw has shaken up the European football landscape, and Feyenoord Rotterdam is among the clubs in the spotlight. The determination of the Dutch side’s opponents in the continent’s premier club competition has generated great interest and put the club under the spotlight.

The Champions League Draw

The group stage of the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 revealed the matchups of European clubs. Feyenoord, one of the Dutch representatives, will face a series of duels ahead, as per the draw held in Monaco. PSV Eindhoven, another Dutch club, will face teams from Madrid, while Feyenoord will travel to Barcelona as part of its journey. The competition, in its 2026/27 edition, follows the same format as last season, with 36 teams participating in the group stage before the best 24 advance to the knockout rounds.

The Challenges for Feyenoord

Feyenoord’s schedule appears more challenging than PSV’s in the main European competition this season. The club will face Barcelona, Internazionale, Como, FC Porto, and RB Leipzig. In addition to playing at home against some of these teams, Feyenoord will travel to face Barcelona, Real Betis, Galatasaray, and Viking. FC Porto, one of the opponents, is currently managed by Francesco Farioli, who lost the Dutch league title to PSV two seasons ago and is now returning to the Netherlands after winning the Portuguese league with Porto.

Return and Ambitions in Europe

Feyenoord returns to the Champions League after participating in the Europa League last season. It is the third time in four seasons that the club enters the main phase of the Champions League. The club hopes to match the result achieved the last time it was in the competition, when it reached the play‑off round before eliminating AC Milan. Additionally, Feyenoord reached the round of 16 in its first attempt in the group stage in 2024/25, demonstrating an ambition for European success.

Changes in Technical Leadership

A second-place finish in the Eredivisie and a direct spot in the UEFA Champions League were not enough for Robin van Persie to keep his position as Feyenoord’s coach. A new administration, formed by Devy Rigaux and Robert Eenhoorn, appointed Giovanni van Bronckhorst as Van Persie’s successor. Van Bronckhorst will embark on his second adventure in the UEFA Champions League with Feyenoord, having finished fourth in Group F in the 2017/18 season. PSV, meanwhile, is the current Eredivisie champion and will see former player Denzel Dumfries face his old club for Real Madrid.
